$comment: Catalog-level UI builder policy for :ha-cards-catalog, the `ha-cards` system: Home Assistant cards in Remote Compose, the palette of the white-labelled builder on ha.coo.ee. Modelled on yschimke/remote-m3-catalog's two policies (remote-catalog's `remote-m3`, widget-catalog's `remote-widgets`). The palette is the HA card components (scalar wrappers over :rc-components' RemoteHa*, HaCardComponents.kt) plus a core of Remote Material 3 re-declared under `ha-cards/` (a catalog cannot extend another). Three design targets share it, told apart by a design's ROOT: the `ha-cards/dashboard-card` builtin (a dashboard card), the Wear widget containers, and the launcher widget. Per-component policy is here rather than on @BuilderComponent stickers, so this file and the templates are one review.

native.reason: The generated Remote Compose Kotlin compiled against this module's own classpath (:rc-components and the alpha Remote Compose + remote-material3 the app ships) and rasterised by the real player — the lane every sticker in this catalog renders through.

$comment_previewSurfaces: No `wasm` surface. The HA components are Android Remote Compose wrappers with no Compose Multiplatform stand-in, so in the browser's Visual Editor they draw as native placeholders (`component.canvas.unclaimed`) until a Wasm runtime for them exists; the Remote Material 3 entries and the heading borrow wear-m3's canvases as remote-m3 does.

frame.$comment_adapter: One frame per catalog, so one adapter for three targets: `frame/widget-host`, remote-m3's — a design is drawn into a host rectangle of a fixed size, which is what a dashboard card slot, a Wear widget container and a launcher cell all are. The sizes list all three; each template sets its own environment size, and the root decides the export (RecordFreeExport: Wear widget container → GlanceWearWidget, `remote-widgets/launcher-widget` → RemoteComposeWidget, else inline RemoteContent).

geometry.$comment: Dashboard cards at the single-column phone width the :previews sheet uses (360dp), short to tall; the two Wear widget containers WearWidgetContainer declares (200x60 and 200x108dp of content plus 8dp padding); and the launcher grid sizes remote-widgets documents, (73n - 16) x (118m - 16) dp.

frame.$comment_previews: Every ha-cards design is a dashboard card that also lands on Wear and the launcher, so the builder previews each one in all three: Samsung's round Wear host at both sizes and the squircle (Pixel Watch) host at large, the launcher grid resized a cell at a time, and the app at phone and tablet column widths. Designs are checked in these panes against docs/design/design-principles.md: content follows area, arrangement follows aspect (half the height and double the width shows the same content, in a row).

$comment_composeSourceExport: The generic Remote Compose emitter, which dispatches on a design's root: a Wear widget container (WEAR_WIDGET_CONTAINER_IDS) exports through WearWidgetCodeExporter, `remote-widgets/launcher-widget` (LauncherWidgetCodeExporter.ROOT) through LauncherWidgetCodeExporter, and anything else — the dashboard card — as inline RemoteContent. Not `remote-compose-launcher-widget`, which would refuse every root but the launcher's.

menu.$comment: This catalog's groups. The three roots lead, then the HA components and the measurement hierarchy (meters and typed readings, card-component-system.md), then the Remote Material 3 core.

$comment_builtins: The design roots, none with a call site of its own. `ha-cards/dashboard-card` exports as HaCardSurface (its `implementation`), which draws the HA card chrome and turns the chrome of the RemoteHa* cards inside it off. `ha-cards/dashboard-section` exports as HaDashboardSection, which draws nothing of its own: the cards under its heading each sit on their own `ha-cards/card-surface`, so they stay separate cards. The Wear widget containers keep remote-m3's ids and the launcher root remote-widgets' id because the export dispatches on those exact ids; nothing checks a builtin's id against this catalog's `ha-cards/` prefix, so they are declared here under their own.
$comment_root_canvas: Dashboard and launcher roots use layout/scaffold because their slot is content. layout/box reads children and would draw these roots empty; builtins cannot declare canvasMapping. This canvas choice does not change their Remote Compose implementation or export target.

properties.name: background
properties.notes: The widget's own background, painted by the host inside the frame it draws: a `#AARRGGBB` literal. Unset is #FF272430, the colour WearWidgetContainer gives a widget that declares none. Padding and corner radius are the host's (WearWidgetParams), so the root never authors them.

properties.name: background
properties.notes: The widget's own background, painted by the host inside the frame it draws: a `#AARRGGBB` literal. Unset is #FF272430, the colour WearWidgetContainer gives a widget that declares none. Padding and corner radius are the host's (WearWidgetParams), so the root never authors them.

properties.name: background
properties.notes: The widget's background, filling the cell the launcher gives it: a `#AARRGGBB` literal, written `RemoteModifier.background(Color(0x…).rc)`. Unset leaves the widget transparent over the wallpaper. The corner radius is the launcher's.

$comment_components: Each `record` names the discovered call (module-relative FQN). The HA components draw as placeholders in the browser canvas (see $comment_previewSurfaces); `icon` keys are HaCardIcons' and HaCardIconsTest holds the two lists together. The Remote Material 3 entries are remote-m3's, minus what only remote-m3's id-keyed emitter can write: text is set by size (no `style` role) and the icon is HA's keyed one rather than RemoteIcon's ImageVector. The `Card layout` group is what a card type's own design (card-designs/ui-builder/designs/<cardType>.uid) is arranged from: switches that pick a slot for the surface and size the card is drawn at, and the forms of a card. Each record is a wrapper over what the card design renderer draws for the same id (HaCardDesignParts.kt), so they draw natively only.

propertyCapabilities.name: theme
propertyCapabilities.notes: A whole look for everything inside: palette, card shape, typeface, how meters are drawn and, for the monochrome themes, one ink. `classic` is the cards' own look; `expressive` Material 3 Expressive (28dp corners, chunky meters with a track gap and stop dot); `trinitron` graphite and tick-scale meters, monospace; `lcd` a segment display with ghost segments (Indiglo backlight in dark mode); `braun` Dieter Rams' warm off-white and hairlines; `nixie` black glass and glowing orange filaments; `console` a skeuomorphic 1970s studio desk (lit hammertone panel, backlit VU meters, metal fader caps, a knob in a lamp ring for dials). `ikea` a furniture showroom (square timber-edged frames, compartment meters, moulded smart-control paddles and opal rings, light and dark). Community-inspired families: `mushroom` petal scales; `bubble` round bead meters; `minimalist` index tabs; `cupertino` concentric rings and filled sliders; `catppuccin` stitched lozenges; `obsidian` ruled scales; `noctis` orbital rails; `lcars` elbow bands; `arctic` horizon needles; `aeon` diamond indexes. All ten have light and dark palettes and retain semantic state colours.

propertyCapabilities.name: dark
propertyCapabilities.notes: The theme's dark mode. A theme with one mode (trinitron, nixie and console are dark only) uses it either way.

propertyCapabilities.name: thresholdsDp
propertyCapabilities.notes: Ascending breakpoints in dp, comma-separated (`56`, `96,180`): N thresholds pick between N+1 tiers, `tier0` below the first.

propertyCapabilities.name: axis
propertyCapabilities.notes: The canvas size the thresholds compare: `width` (a launcher cell) or `height` (a Wear container).

propertyCapabilities.name: scale
propertyCapabilities.notes: `row` sizes it for a one-row launcher cell; `wear` for a Wear container, without features and not live.

propertyCapabilities.name: minWidthDp
propertyCapabilities.notes: The narrowest canvas, in dp, that takes `roomy`.

propertyCapabilities.name: minHeightDp
propertyCapabilities.notes: The shortest canvas, in dp, that takes `roomy`.

propertyCapabilities.name: compact
propertyCapabilities.notes: `grid` draws the compact body in a square grid cell only, `true` always, `false` never.

propertyCapabilities.name: inset
propertyCapabilities.notes: `card` insets the row by a card's horizontal padding, for a cell that is the card; `none` doesn't.

propertyCapabilities.name: scale
propertyCapabilities.notes: `row` sizes it for a one-row launcher cell; `wear` for a Wear container, not live.

$comment_newDesign: The catalog label appears in the New design chooser. Its templates come in three groups, which a host offering only this catalog shows as the choices: Dashboard section (a heading over several cards), Card (one Home Assistant card) and Component (a building block cards are made of). Wear and launcher widgets are sizes and roots a design can take, not starting points, so no template asks.
